## Goal

Measure which skills and canon rules are actually used -- by which agent/runtime, in which repo, how often -- so a weekly review can rotate skills in and out of the global list, move single-project skills into their owning repo, shelve rarely-used ones as on-demand, and retire dead ones. Operator (Rico) approved 2026-08-01, and placed it ON the rewrite path: "We're rewriting it, so this seems like a good place to add new functionality."

## Existing design this builds on (do NOT reinvent)

- entry_access_log table: src/db/migrations/006_cognitive_tiering.sql -- per-access rows (entry, agent, query/source, time).
- access_count / last_accessed_at / usefulness_score rollups on entry tables: src/db/migrations/002_curation.sql.
- access_report tool: src/tools/access-report.ts -- total accesses, unique queries, unique agents, trend, recency per entry.
- tier_recommendations and list_stale tools already turn usage into prioritization.
- Gotcha: 008_index_cleanup.sql dropped all three non-PK indexes on entry_access_log with note "write-only table, 0 scans" -- the log has never been read. Re-add an index only when the weekly report actually reads it and measurement shows the need.

## Delta scope, split across the two rewrite halves

### Python side (belongs with the remaining Python-apps work, sibling of apps/hooks)

1. Harness emitter: Claude Code PostToolUse hook on the Skill tool captures {skill, agent, repo, session} and writes through the existing provider path into entry_access_log. Codex and Pi equivalents come later through their own hook chains.

### Server/TS side (folds into the server rewrite charting, issue #463)

2. Seed one OB entity per skill, keyed skill.<slug> (same scope-key pattern as canon seeding), so the access log has rows to point at.
3. Weekly metrics section: add skill-usage telemetry as a section of Rico's existing Sunday 08:00 Weekly Round-Up, not as a standalone report or new job. Existing mechanism: `/Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/_ob/bin/weeklyroundup` (`weeklyroundup email`), scheduled by launchd label `com.rtech.weekly-roundup`. The section is factual metrics only:
   - invocation counts per skill x agent x repo x runtime;
   - trend versus prior weeks;
   - last-used timestamps;
   - an explicit never-used list.

   It must never categorize, recommend, rotate, shelve, or retire anything. Rico makes those decisions from the facts: "no automatic retirement. What I need is something that gives me metrics so that decisions can be made on facts and not on feel."
4. Same telemetry answers which canon rules load where, feeding the router dedupe work (PR #468).

## Out of scope

Dream changes, automatic rotation, automatic categorization, recommendations, retirement, anything on core01 until proven locally.

## Sequencing

This is ON the rewrite path per operator decision. The Python emitter piece sequences with the remaining Python work; the server-side seed/report piece sequences with the server rewrite #463. It belongs in the rewrite-path sequence on map #443, not the nice-to-have lane.
